# t008 source verification notes (retrieved 2026-10-09)

## 7 Fiore & Leinster — VERIFIED_SOURCE
arXiv:math/0508617v2 (13 Jan 2010), "An abstract characterization of Thompson's group F", Thm 1.1 (p.2).
"Theorem 1.1 Let A be the monoidal category freely generated by an idempotent object (A, α). Then Aut_A(A) is isomorphic to Thompson's group F." 'idempotent object' = object A with iso α: A⊗A → A.
Also: "the monoidal category freely generated by an object A and an isomorphism A ⊗ A → A is equivalent to the groupoid 1 ∐ F". NOTE: monoidal (not symmetric) and group F (not V).

## 10 Scherer — VERIFIED_SOURCE
arXiv:1610.01213v3 [cs.PL] 8 Nov 2016, "Deciding equivalence with sums and the empty type". System: simply-typed λ-calculus ΛC(X,→,×,1,+,0) (atoms, functions, pairs, unit, sums, empty). Contributions (§1.4): "βη-equivalence is decidable"; "βη-equivalence and contextual equivalence coincide". Corollary 7: "Equivalence in the full simply-typed λ-calculus with sums and the empty type is decidable." Intro: prior non-empty-sum decidability Ghani 1995, Lindley 2007, Altenkirch–Dybjer–Hofmann–Scott 2001, Balat–Di Cosmo–Fiore 2004; "Decidability in the presence of the empty type is still open – we propose a proof." The paper phrases result for the λ-calculus, not literally "free bicartesian closed category" (categorical link only via a remark/"we wonder" in conclusion). Peer-reviewed POPL 2017 version NOT_ACCESSED.

## 8 Uemura — VERIFIED_SOURCE
arXiv:1904.04097v3 (26 May 2023). Def 4.1 stable class of exponentiable arrows (contains ids, closed under composition, pullback-stable, exponentiable). Def 4.2: "A representable map category consists of: a cartesian category C; a stable class of exponentiable arrows of C" (representable arrows). Representable map functor: preserves finite limits, representable arrows, pushforwards along representable arrows. Def 4.4 "A type theory is a small representable map category." Def 4.5 model: small category S with terminal object + representable map functor T → DFib_S. Def 3.18 pushforward = right adjoint of pullback f* (dependent product along f). Type formers given in a logical framework signature (Sec 5), e.g. Example 5.8 Π-types: constants Π, abs, app with β equation app(abs b, a)=ba and η/extensionality equation (pointwise-equal b,b' ⇒ b=b'). So universal properties are specified by symbols+equations in the LF, whose syntactic RMC has a universal property (Thm 5.17).

## 5 Lawvere — VERIFIED_SOURCE
TAC Reprints No.16 (2006) pp.1–16, orig. Dialectica 23 (1969). p.3: "One of the aims of this paper is to give evidence for the universality of the concept of adjointness, which ... also seems to pervade logic. ... The structure of a cartesian closed category is entirely given by adjointness, as is the structure of a 'hyperdoctrine', which includes quantification as well." p.11–12 (hyperdoctrine item 4): Σf and Πf "equipped with adjunctions that make them respectively left and right adjoint to substitution f"; "the existential (respectively universal) quantification of ϕ along f". Author commentary p.1: logical operations "characterized as local adjoints" of substitution.

## 3 Pfenning & Davies — VERIFIED_SOURCE (preprint)
https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~fp/papers/mscs00.pdf (header "Under consideration for publication in Math. Struct. in Comp. Science", Received May 2000), pp.3–4. "We only consider each elimination immediately preceded by an introduction for a connective. We therefore call the property that each such pattern can be reduced local soundness." "we say that the elimination rules for a connective are locally complete if we can apply the elimination rules to a judgment to recover enough knowledge to permit reconstruction of the original judgment." "Local soundness and completeness are witnessed by local reductions and expansions of proofs, respectively." Word "harmony" not used in this passage. Published MSCS 11(4) 2001 version pagination NOT_ACCESSED.

## 2/9 Girard–Lafont–Taylor, Proofs and Types — VERIFIED_SOURCE
https://www.paultaylor.eu/stable/prot.pdf (CUP 1989, "Reprinted for the Web 2003").
§11.3.2 p.83–84: U×V = ΠX.(U→V→X)→X; projections compute by β; "Note that ⟨π1 t, π2 t⟩ ⇝ t does not hold, even if we allow λx^U. t x ⇝ t and ΛX. t X ⇝ t." (surjective pairing fails even with η)
§11.3.4 p.84–85: U+V = ΠX.(U→X)→(V→X)→X; "the translation does not interpret the commuting or secondary conversions associated with the sum type; the same remark applies to the type Emp and also to the type Bool". §11.3.3 Emp=ΠX.X.
§3 p.20 (simply typed λ with ×): equations incl. η and surjective pairing; "Theorem The system given by these equations is consistent and decidable."
Ch.14 p.113: "Theorem All terms of F are strongly normalisable, and the normal form is unique." — β only (reductions of §11.1: λ-β and (ΛX.v)U ⇝ v[U/X]); no η. Hence decidability of β-equality for F follows (normalize & compare) — decidability of βη for F is NOT stated in this source.
§11.2 p.82: ΛX.λx^X.x of type ΠX.X→X "the identity of any type" (no uniqueness/parametricity claim there).

(Page note for P&T: pdf pages — simply-typed "consistent and decidable" theorem pdf p.24 (§3.3-ish, printed p.16); §11.3.2 note pdf p.92 (printed p.84); §11.3.4 remark pdf p.93 (printed p.85); Ch14 theorem pdf p.121 (printed p.113).)

## 1 Reynolds 1983 — VERIFIED_SOURCE via OCR (scan; OCR noise)
https://people.mpi-sws.org/~dreyer/tor/papers/reynolds.pdf = Information Processing 83 (IFIP), pp.513–523. p.516 "Abstraction Theorem Let R be a relation assignment between set assignments S1 and S2 ... In essence, the semantics of any expression maps related environments into related values." Setting: Reynolds' set-theoretic semantics of typed λ-calculus (later shown impossible for polymorphism, per Wadler). p.520: "The abstraction theorem guarantees that, in an environment in which all polymorphic functions are parametric, the meaning of any ordinary expression will be parametric." Reynolds does NOT state "∀X.X→X has only identity" in retrieved text.

## 1 Wadler 1989 — VERIFIED_SOURCE via OCR
https://people.mpi-sws.org/~dreyer/tor/papers/wadler.pdf ("slightly revised version", June 1989, of FPCA'89). p.1–2: "Parametricity is just a reformulation of Reynolds' abstraction theorem: terms evaluated in related environments yield related values". p.2: "This paper uses the frame models of Bruce, Meyer, and Mitchell"; Reynolds' naive set-theoretic models "do not exist [Rey84]". p.3 Prop: "(Parametricity.) If t is a closed term of type T, then (t,t) ∈ T, where T is the relation corresponding to the type T." Sec 6 p.~10: formal version "if X;Γ ⊢ t:T then X;Γ ⊨ t:T", proof by induction on typing. Fig.1: I: ∀X.X→X gives a ∘ I_A = I_A' ∘ a (for every function a). "Only identity" is a corollary, not stated verbatim. Sec 7: with fixpoints relations must be strict & continuous; only strict functions usable as relations ("if fixpoints are allowed then the [theorem is weakened]").

## 1/2 Plotkin–Abadi — VERIFIED_SOURCE (venue UNVERIFIED-MEMORY: TLCA'93, LNCS 664)
https://homepages.inf.ed.ac.uk/gdp/publications/Par_Poly.pdf. Logic over System F with β and η equality axioms plus parametricity schema. §3.1 (pdf p.9): 1 = ∀X.X→X; "It is provable, using dinaturality, that: Theorem 1 ∀u:1.(u =1 ⋆)" [⋆ = ΛX λx:X.x]. A×B = ∀Z.((A→B→Z)→Z) "yields a weak product in System F"; β laws "provable without using parametricity"; "Using dinaturality we obtain: Theorem 2 ∀w:A×B.(⟨fst(w),snd(w)⟩ = w)". Theorem 4 ∀u:0.⊥; Theorem 5 (pdf p.10) ∀Z∀h:A+B→Z. h=[inl;h,inr;h]_Z (η for sums). Dinaturality schema stated as consequence of binary relational parametricity schema (p.~2). Also: Mitchell [Mit90] "two terms of the same type are equal in a wide class of [PER] models iff their erasures are βη-equivalent".

## 2 Hasegawa — VERIFIED_SOURCE
LMCS 2(3:3) 2006, arXiv cs/0606072v2. Abstract: "the unconstrained relational parametricity on the λµ-calculus turns out to be inconsistent". Prop 4.1 (pdf p.9): consequences of parametricity in target λ2. §4.4 (pdf p.10): lists ⊤=∀X.X→X, ∧, ∨, ∃ encodings; "although ⊤ is not a terminal object in λµ2, it has a unique closed inhabitant." Adversarial: parametricity-based η for Church encodings fails to transfer to control/classical calculi without "focal" restriction.

## 2 Tranchini–Pistone–Petrolo — VERIFIED_SOURCE
arXiv:1607.06603v2 "The naturality of natural deduction". Abstract: Prawitz "showed how the usual natural deduction inference rules for disjunction, conjunction and absurdity can be derived using those for implication and the second order quantifier" in NI2; "the translation does not preserve the relations of identity among derivations induced by the permutative conversions and immediate expansions ... when the equational theory of NI2 is assumed to consist only of β and η equations." p.7: β-equivalence preserved; for η and γ (permutative) not, "actually not even D1* =βη D2*". Def 2.1 (A∨B)* ≡ ∀X((A*⊃X)⊃(B*⊃X)⊃X). Proposes naturality equations (generalized permutation) under which RP translation preserves identity. Prawitz 1965 itself: NOT_ACCESSED (SECONDARY_ONLY via this paper + P&T §11.3).

## 9 βη for System F
- Abel, "Weak βη-Normalization and Normalization by Evaluation for System F" (LPAR 2008; https://www.cse.chalmers.se/~abela/lpar08.pdf) — VERIFIED_SOURCE: Thm 4 (pdf p.10) "If Γ ⊢ t : A then t β-reduces η-expands to a long normal form t′"; §7 nf "maps exactly the βη-equal terms of the same type to the same η-long β-normal form"; complete & sound; Thm 6 (p.13) Completeness of NbE. Decidability of βη then follows (paper does not use word "decidable" for it — inference).
- Ghani, "Eta Expansions in System F", LIENS-96-10 — VERIFIED_SOURCE (Greek glyphs lost in extraction; reconstructed): β-rewrite "well-known to be both strongly normalising, confluent [10] and hence [β]-equality is decidable in System F"; abstract: proves SN and confluence for β-reductions + restricted η-expansions, normal forms = long βη-normal forms; abstract says expansionary rules give "decidability of [βη]-equality".

## 4 Structurality — VERIFIED_SOURCE
SEP "Algebraic Propositional Logic" (Ramon Jansana; first pub. 12 Dec 2016, rev. 20 May 2022), §2: logic system = language + consequence relation "formal in the sense that for every substitution σ, ... if Γ ⊢ φ, then σ[Γ] ⊢ σ(φ)". "The consequence relations ... that satisfy this property are called structural and also substitution-invariant in the literature. They were considered for the first time in Łoś & Suszko 1958." Ref: Łoś & Suszko 1958, "Remarks on sentential logics", Indag. Math. 61:177–183 (citation from SEP; original NOT_ACCESSED). NB: SEP builds it into definition of 'logic', not an iff theorem.

## 3b Inversion/harmony — VERIFIED_SOURCE (secondary for Prawitz)
SEP "Proof-Theoretic Semantics" (Schroeder-Heister; rev. 18 Aug 2023) §2.2.1 quotes Prawitz 1965 p.33 inversion principle: "Let α be an application of an elimination rule that has B as consequence. Then, deductions that satisfy the sufficient condition [...] for deriving the major premiss of α, when combined with deductions of the minor premisses of α (if any), already 'contain' a deduction of B". Notes harmony terminology "not uniform"; tonk excluded; "Formal characterizations of harmony have used the translation of inference rules into second-order propositional logic (Girard's system F)". General elimination rules (Schroeder-Heister 1984 / Read 2010): only mentioned by name — not verified in detail.
